entries.why_context_sensitive: Explicit @ forces implicit intersection of the column range A1:A3 against the caller's row. The result depends on the caller location relative to the range, which only exists in a bound worksheet context.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller on row 1, implicit intersection of A1:A3 picks the value on the caller's row: 10.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Explicit @ over a row range intersects against the caller's column. The picked element depends on caller column, a bound-context fact.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller in column E (outside A:C on the same row), Excel returns #VALUE! because the implicit intersection has no overlapping column. Caller column within A:C returns that column's value.

entries.why_context_sensitive: SEQUENCE(3) yields a dynamic-array column; explicit @ collapses it by implicit intersection against the caller row. Requires dynamic-array evaluation plus caller-relative intersection.
entries.expected_behavior: With the caller on row 1, @ on the 3-tall array {1;2;3} returns the caller-row element: 1.

entries.why_context_sensitive: OFFSET returns a reference (a 3x1 range A2:A4); explicit @ then implicitly intersects it against the caller. Both the reference transform and the intersection are context-bound.
entries.expected_behavior: OFFSET(A1,1,0,3,1) is A2:A4; @ against caller row 1 has no overlap, so Excel returns #VALUE!. A caller row within rows 2-4 returns that row's value.

entries.why_context_sensitive: OFFSET produces a derived reference from a base cell and offsets; SUM then enumerates the derived range. The reference transform requires a resolver that can offset a real reference, which OxFunc does not own in isolation.

INDEX with row_num 0 returns the entire column 2 as a reference (B1:B3), not a scalar. SUM then enumerates that derived reference. The reference-returning form of INDEX is a reference transform the OxFunc provider does not resolve without binding.
entries.expected_behavior: INDEX(A1:C3,0,2) is the reference B1:B3; SUM = 2+5+8 = 15.

entries.why_context_sensitive: INDIRECT builds a reference from runtime text and resolves it against the workbook. Resolving the assembled A1-style string to a live cell requires host reference resolution.
entries.expected_behavior: B1 is 2, so the text is "A2"; INDIRECT("A2") dereferences A2 = 22.

entries.why_context_sensitive: CELL reports host-level metadata (address, format, sheet) about a reference. The answer is a property of the workbook/host, not of any value OxFunc can compute alone.
entries.expected_behavior: CELL("address",A1) returns the absolute address text "$A$1".

entries.why_context_sensitive: FORMULATEXT returns the literal formula string of the referenced cell, which only exists in a workbook that stores formulas. OxFunc evaluates values, not stored formula text.
entries.expected_behavior: A1 stores =1+2, so FORMULATEXT(A1) returns the text "=1+2".

entries.why_context_sensitive: Table1[Amount] is a structured reference resolved against a workbook table definition (header row, body range, current region). Resolving the column to a range requires the table model.
entries.expected_behavior: The Amount column is {100;250;75}; SUM = 425.

entries.why_context_sensitive: The operand lives on a different sheet. Resolving Sheet2!A1:A3 requires a multi-sheet workbook model the local OxFunc resolver does not carry.
entries.expected_behavior: Sum of Sheet2!A1:A3 = 6000.

entries.why_context_sensitive: A1# is the spill-range reference anchored at A1. Its extent is determined by what the A1 dynamic-array formula spilled, which only exists after the workbook recalculates the anchor.
entries.expected_behavior: A1 spills {1;2;3}; A1# is A1:A3; SUM = 6.

entries.why_context_sensitive: BYROW binds an inline LAMBDA and invokes it per row. Forming and invoking the callable is formula-binding scope owned by the OxFml binder, not the OxFunc value surface in isolation.
entries.expected_behavior: Row sums spill as a 2x1 column {3;7}.

entries.why_context_sensitive: LET introduces named bindings into formula scope before evaluating the body. The name-binding step is OxFml formula-binding scope, not a pure function call.
entries.expected_behavior: x=6, y=7, body x*y = 42.

entries.why_context_sensitive: VALUE parses text to a number through a LocaleFormatContext parser (value_fn.rs). OxFunc does not ship a local locale parser; the capability bundle is supplied through the typed seam (W082). Without it, VALUE("2") returns #VALUE! locally. This row was reclassified from a Category-2 probe to Category 1 on the first run of the evaluation-class lane (W104), demonstrating the classifier.
entries.expected_behavior: With a locale capability bundle supplied downstream, VALUE("2") returns the number 2.
entries.status: M1 tested (locally) — locale seam; OxFunc returns #VALUE! without the locale capability bundle.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Same-sheet multi-area reference; SUM enumerates both areas. Resolving the combined reference is OxFunc resolver combination semantics over a real workbook.
entries.expected_behavior: Sum across both areas = 10.
entries.status: HO downstream — OxFunc-side MultiArea identity + Style-A materialization corrected (W075/W076); HO-FN-006/007 downstream acknowledgement pending.

entries.why_context_sensitive: TAKE preserves a 1x1 array internally (TYPE(...)=64); whether a 1x1 spill publishes as a scalar or a 1x1 array is decided by the downstream worksheet publication/comparator, not by the function.
entries.expected_behavior: TAKE({1,2;3,4},1,1) is a 1x1 array containing 1; final-cell publication shape is a downstream concern.
entries.status: HO downstream — function-level scalarization reverted; HO-FN-010 filed for the OxFml/DNA Calc publication seam.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Locale-aware text->number parse; depends on the W082 locale-format capability bundle OxFunc does not own locally.
entries.expected_behavior: NUMBERVALUE("2") = 2 (with the locale bundle).
entries.status: M1 tested — locale parse seam (cluster: VALUE, NUMBERVALUE, DATEVALUE, TIMEVALUE). NOTE: the error-propagation aspect DATEVALUE(NA())->#N/A is Category 2 and is tracked in OXFUNC_EXCEL_DISCREPANCY_CATALOG G2.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Locale-aware date-text->serial parse; depends on the W082 locale-format/date-system capability bundle.
entries.expected_behavior: DATEVALUE of an ISO date returns its 1900-system serial (with the locale/date bundle).
entries.status: M1 tested — locale date-parse seam (TIMEVALUE shares it).

entries.why_context_sensitive: Locale-aware number->text formatting; depends on the W082 locale-format capability bundle (separators, currency).
entries.expected_behavior: TEXT formats per the locale's group/decimal separators and the supplied format code.
entries.status: M1 tested — locale format seam (cluster: TEXT, DOLLAR, FIXED).

entries.why_context_sensitive: Full-width<->half-width (DBCS) conversion; depends on the locale/DBCS capability OxFunc does not own locally.
entries.expected_behavior: ASC converts full-width characters to half-width per the DBCS locale.
entries.status: M1 tested — DBCS/locale seam (cluster: ASC, DBCS, JIS).

entries.why_context_sensitive: HYPERLINK is a host/UI surface; its published value and behavior depend on the host, not a pure computation.
entries.expected_behavior: Returns the friendly-name text and registers a host hyperlink; behavior is host-defined.
entries.status: M0 noted — host seam; needs a host-fixture decision before comparison is meaningful.

entries.why_context_sensitive: TRIMRANGE returns a reference trimmed of surrounding blank rows/columns; the result is a reference transform over a real workbook range.
entries.expected_behavior: Returns the inner non-blank sub-range of A1:D10.
entries.status: M0 noted — reference-transform seam; needs a workbook fixture.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Nested TYPE evidence classifies MINVERSE(5) as a 1x1 array; Excel's final worksheet cell displays its scalar anchor value. That final publication/comparator choice is downstream of the OxFunc function result.
entries.expected_behavior: MINVERSE(5) remains a 1x1 array containing 0.2 internally; final-cell scalar-versus-array publication is a downstream concern.
entries.status: HO downstream — function-level scalarization reverted; HO-FN-010 filed for the OxFml/DNA Calc publication seam.

entries.why_context_sensitive: Nested TYPE evidence classifies MMULT(5,2) as a 1x1 array; Excel's final worksheet cell displays its scalar anchor value. That final publication/comparator choice is downstream of the OxFunc function result.
entries.expected_behavior: MMULT(5,2) remains a 1x1 array containing 10 internally; final-cell scalar-versus-array publication is a downstream concern.
entries.status: HO downstream — function-level scalarization reverted; HO-FN-010 filed for the OxFml/DNA Calc publication seam.
